metadata.topic: Optics — Converging Lens: Image Distance and Magnification

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q5d — Converging Lens: Image Distance and Magnification
question.text:
A converging lens has a focal length f = 10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm from the lens.

Calculate:

  1. The image distance v (4 marks)
  2. The magnification produced (2 marks)
question.general_feedback:
(i) Image distance:
Lens formula: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30
v = 30 cm (real, inverted image)

(ii) Magnification:
m = v/u = 30/15 = 2

Note: Since v > 0 and m > 0 (using real-is-positive convention), the image is real, inverted, and magnified.

steps.label:
Given: f = 10 cm  |  u = 15 cm (object distance)
Lens formula: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u    Magnification: m = v/u
Part (i) — Calculate the image distance v using the lens formula. (4 marks)

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Lens formula: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u (not 1/f + 1/u). Subtract the reciprocal of the object distance from the reciprocal of the focal length.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: v = 1 ÷ (1/30) = 30 cm. Take the reciprocal of your answer for 1/v.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Magnification formula: m = v/u (image distance divided by object distance).
